content.text: Investigation complete. My searches for every detection signal — "compet" (only "court of competent jurisdiction"), "shall not engage"/"will not engage", "exclusiv" (only Cap Collateral Account control), "solicit", "territory", and "restrict" — returned no non-compete or field-of-use covenant. I read Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article V (Depositor) in full: the only negative covenants binding our side are structural securitization provisions (no transfer or lien on Transferred Property, no petition, no division, maintain existence), none of which limit what businesses we may operate or what products we may buy or build.

input.quote: Except for the transfer and assignment under this Agreement, the Depositor will not transfer or assign any Depositor Transferred Property to another Person or Grant or allow a Lien, other than a Permitted Lien, on an interest in any Depositor Transferred Property.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binding the Issuer or the Depositor, which meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer). Searches for "compet" returned only "court of competent jurisdiction" (p0335, p0469); "shall not/will not engage", "solicit" and "territory" returned nothing; and "exclusiv" returned only the Cap Collateral Account control mechanics (p0387-p0388) and the non-exclusive jurisdiction clause (p0427). Article IX (Other Agreements) and Article X (Miscellaneous), the only plausible homes, contain no restrictive covenant on our business activities. The negative covenants that do bind our side are structural securitization provisions rather than vendor protections: Section 9.2's bar on transferring or encumbering the Depositor Transferred Property (p0372), Section 5.7's no-division covenant (p0253) and Section 9.5's no-petition covenant (p0377), none of which limit the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. Consistent with the rule's guidance, Permitted Activities limits on the Issuer arise under the Trust Agreement and structural covenants and are not treated as a non-compete. No redline required.
